title: Matrix ultraviolet-shell Cauchy bound for arbitrary Gaussian covariance

matrix_shell_cost.spectral_data: Let Omega=diag(omega_j), Lambda=diag(lambda_j) with lambda_j=(2omega_j)^(-1), and let P_N be the fixed-ratio ultraviolet-shell projector from K1525; then C_(S,N)=Tr(P_N Lambda)>=kappa C_N and P_N commutes with Omega and Lambda
matrix_shell_cost.integrated_variance: For arbitrary S>0, V_N=Tr(Lambda S)>=Tr(P_N Lambda S)>=0
matrix_shell_cost.low_variance_deficit: If V_N<=(kappa/2)C_N, then delta_N=Tr[P_N Lambda(I-S)]>=kappa C_N/2=Theta(N^2)
matrix_shell_cost.frobenius_factorization: Set A=Omega^(1/2)(I-S)S^(-1/2) and B=S^(1/2)P_N Lambda Omega^(-1/2); cyclicity gives Tr(AB)=delta_N
matrix_shell_cost.matrix_cauchy: Frobenius Cauchy gives delta_N^2<=Tr[Omega(S+S^(-1)-2I)] Tr[P_N Lambda^2 Omega^(-1)P_N S]
matrix_shell_cost.dual_shell_bound: On the shell, P_N Lambda^2 Omega^(-1)P_N<=cN^(-2)P_N Lambda in Loewner order, hence the second factor is at most cN^(-2)Tr(P_N Lambda S)<=cN^(-2)V_N=O(1)
matrix_shell_cost.free_cost_consequence: The covariance part of K1528's q0 is one quarter of the first factor, so q0>=cN^4 in the low-integrated-variance branch
matrix_shell_cost.high_variance_consequence: If V_N>(kappa/2)C_N, K1529 gives interaction expectation at least g c_* C_N V_N>=c_g C_N^2=c_gN^4
matrix_shell_cost.noncommutative_guard: No step assumes that S commutes with Omega, Lambda or P_N; off-diagonal shell/complement correlations are retained in the positive matrix traces
matrix_shell_cost.scope_guard: The dichotomy covers arbitrary positive Gaussian covariance at finite cutoff, not a non-Gaussian density or a cutoff-uniform continuum representation
